args.sql:
with f as (select customer, store_id, ordered_at, row_number() over (partition by customer order by ordered_at, id) rn, count(*) over (partition by customer, ordered_at) ties from orders),
first as (select customer, store_id, ties from f where rn=1),
spend as (select customer, sum(subtotal) s from orders group by customer)
select st.name, count(*) n, sum(s)/100.0/count(*) avg_spend, sum(case when ties>1 then 1 else 0 end) tied, (select count(*) from orders where customer is null) nullcust
from first join spend using(customer) left join stores st on st.id=first.store_id group by st.name order by n desc

args.sql:
with f as (select customer, store_id, ordered_at, row_number() over (partition by customer order by ordered_at, id) rn, count(*) over (partition by customer, ordered_at) nt from orders),
fo as (select customer, store_id, nt from f where rn=1),
spend as (select customer, sum(subtotal) s from orders group by customer)
select st.name, count(*) n, sum(s)/100.0/count(*) avg_spend, sum(case when nt>1 then 1 else 0 end) tied, (select count(*) from orders where customer is null) nullcust
from fo join spend using(customer) left join stores st on st.id=fo.store_id group by st.name order by n desc

args.message: Each customer is assigned to the store where they placed their first order. No customer had two orders tied for the earliest time. Lifetime spend is pre-tax (orders.subtotal in cents, divided by 100) and covers all of the customer's orders at any store, all dates included. Philadelphia has the highest average ($6,389) and Los Angeles the lowest ($1,220). Stores that opened later have had less time to build up lifetime spend: New Orleans opened Apr 2025 and Los Angeles Oct 2025, so their averages aren't directly comparable to the older stores.
